Name: Hallows_Eve_Gravekeeper
$Comment: The Gravekeeper's conversation, what pressing F on him opens in the Forgotten Temple while
Hallow's Eve runs. He is one of the Hallowed and keeps the Headless Horseman's graveyard for them,
so his own lines name neither Old Jack nor Hallow's Eve as his reason to be there: Jack comes up
only as the man who sells the candles his gate burns, and on the ember line, shown to a player on
Old Jack's errand, as the one who sent them. He never contracts: I am, it is, does not. That keeps
him apart from Old Jack, who always does.
HOW A SCREEN IS PICKED. First is walked top to bottom, then Fallback. The ember line comes first,
while the player carries Old Jack's hard step (hallows_eve_old_jack_horseman_hard): it says the
ember only drops on the hard ride. Then the hard ride's introduction, once per character
(OnceId hard_open), for a player who has finished The Rider (hallows_eve_old_jack_horseman).
Every other visit opens on menu.
THE MENU. gk_menu is on every screen a visit opens on: take me in (the normal graveyard), take me
on the hard ride (the hard graveyard, shown only to a player who has finished The Rider; this
condition is the hard graveyard's only quest gate, since the dungeon itself asks only for its
season and its candle, so no other line or press-F may open it), who he is, and goodnight. Each
way in is the Dungeon destination, which sends the player in with their party, or says why it
refused. The who screen carries gk_back: back to the menu, or goodnight. The trick-or-treat line
is not here: the DialogueExtensions file Hallows_Eve_Trick_Or_Treat adds it to every
conversation, this one included, and its favor goes to the Hallowed, his own people.
THE PRICE. Each graveyard's EntryCost (ZiggfreedCommon/Dungeons) takes its candle from whoever
opens an area for their party: a Grave Candle for the graveyard, a Burning Grave Candle for the
hard ride. The menu line says the gate wants a Grave Candle and the hard ride's introduction and
the ember line name the Burning one, each saying Old Jack sells it; each way-in label shows its
price. Option labels take no number from the file, so a changed count is written into both labels
in every language. Picking a way in opens CommonLib's confirm screen in this page's place (the
dungeon's EntryCost.Confirm, built like the game's portal summon screen): the graveyard's name and
description, the candle, how many the player holds and how many it takes, and Light the Candle,
which burns it and sends the party in. With too few, the button is off and the screen says where
Old Jack sells them, and nothing is spent. A partymate following into a graveyard their party
already holds skips the screen and walks in free.
